title: Two papers disagree (diet-and-mortality)
explanation: Claim A finds that alcohol consumption significantly reduces all-cause mortality risk, whereas Claim B finds no significant reduction in mortality risk after controlling for abstainer biases and study quality.
a_text: Alcohol consumption is associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality compared with non-drinking (pooled adjusted RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.83 to 0.92).
b_text: After adjusting for abstainer biases and study quality characteristics, low-volume alcohol consumption shows no significant reduction in mortality risk.

audit.reason: Same paper pair and same topic as the pair immediately above (BMJ 2011 vs Stockwell 2016 alcohol/mortality). The other Claim B here is a near-identical restatement of the abstainer-bias correction. Counted once.
